1. Case 1: Lung cancer progression
Severe dyspnea and dry cough in a smoker with treated lung cancer point to recurrence. CTPA showing a mediastinal mass compressing both pulmonary arteries plus right heart enlargement explains the symptoms and murmur. No embolus on CTPA rules out thromboembolism. Right heart strain is secondary cor pulmonale, but absent leg edema argues against advanced right heart failure. Pleural effusion/atelectasis is less likely given imaging. Since biopsy pathology and tumor markers are pending, histologic confirmation is lacking; thus lung cancer progression is the leading diagnosis, with moderate-high confidence.

Here is the reference diagnosis for this case:
1. Case 1: Mediastinal metastasis of lung cancer with bilateral pulmonary artery stenosis
